message.content:
I don’t have real‑time data, but you can quickly check the current air quality in Los Angeles by visiting one of the following resources:

| Source | What it offers | How to use |
|--------|----------------|------------|
| **AirNow** (airnow.gov) | Live AQI (Air Quality Index) for all U.S. cities, including Los Angeles. | Search “Los Angeles” → see the current AQI, pollutant levels (PM₂.₅, O₃, NO₂, etc.), and health recommendations. |
| **EPA’s Air Quality Dashboard** | Historical and current data, maps, and trend analysis. | Navigate to the “Air Quality” section → select “Los Angeles” or the specific ZIP code. |
| **Local news sites** (e.g., LA Times, KABC) | Often publish brief updates during smog events. | Look for “air quality” or “smog alert” in the news feed. |
| **Weather apps** (e.g., Weather.com, AccuWeather) | Many include an AQI widget. | Open the app → search for Los Angeles → view the AQI card. |

If you’re planning outdoor activities, the AQI categories are:

- **0–50** – Good  
- **51–100** – Moderate  
- **101–150** – Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups  
- **151–200** – Unhealthy  
- **201–300** – Very Unhealthy  
- **301+** – Hazardous  

Check the current AQI and follow any health advisories if it’s above “Moderate.”
